questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the bus driver should:

options.text: Not use their mirrors.
Slow down and be careful.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver must always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the fifth wheel locking jaws are completely closed around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:

options.text: Be in a single-file line.
Be in pairs.
Not use the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly and in a single-file line. They should hold the handrail for safety.

questions.question: When dropping off students at school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition when leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine when unloading students. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave your seat. Stay and watch while students exit.

questions.question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you begin your trip.

questions.question: If your bus has a roof-mounted strobe light, use it:

options.text: When you cannot see well.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cannot see well.
questions.explanation: Use the roof-mounted strobe light when there is limited visibility.

questions.question: When students are picked up by a school bus:

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should pick up students anywhere they are waiting.
Parents should choose where the bus stop will be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: Load and unload students only at approved designated stops chosen by the school district.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be dangerous for passengers.
Should be supervised by someone other than the driver.
Should be done while refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: Passengers can fall when getting on or off the bus. Tell passengers to watch their step when exiting.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only when all other seats are full.
Sit as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only when all other seats are full.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Sitting toward the front is safer in a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: When loading or unloading passengers and there is no park shift point, put the bus in:

options.text: Reverse
First gear
Neutral

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral
questions.explanation: Put the bus in park when loading or unloading students. If park is not available, put it in neutral and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If a bus must be evacuated, where is it safest for students to stand?

options.text: No more than 50 feet away from the bus.
Downwind of the bus in case of fire.
Far away from any railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Far away from any railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: After leaving a bus, students should go to a safe place at least 100 feet from the road, facing oncoming traffic. This protects them from debris if another vehicle hits the bus. Students should stay upwind of fires and far from railroad tracks.

questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check all mirrors for students running toward the bus.
Count the students at the bus stop and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: When arriving at a bus stop, the driver should count students and make sure they all board. The driver should check mirrors for students running to the stop. Students should board slowly in a single line, not in pairs.

questions.question: When a school bus approaches a bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use the mirrors.
Approach slowly and carefully.
Drive quickly and stop suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: An encroachment is when:

options.text: A driver misses their scheduled basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one part of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens during the basic skills test when any part of the vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must check all of the following, except:

options.text: The power steering belt.
The water compressor belt.
The alternator belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water compressor belt.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if the vehicle has them. The water compressor belt is not checked.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces are still grooved.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are still grooved.
questions.explanation: When checking pedals during a pre-trip inspection, make sure nothing blocks them. Check that pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces if they should.

questions.question: If you come to railroad tracks while driving a school bus, you should:

options.text: Check the tracks and continue driving without stopping.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should stop before railroad crossings to check for trains. Stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail to see the tracks clearly. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: Watch passengers inside the bus.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror in a school bus is used to monitor what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: As a general rule, where should students stay during an emergency?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the bus
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control if kept on the bus. However, if staying on the bus puts students at risk, the driver should move them to a safe location.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, the driver should ensure all traffic has stopped before:

options.text: Opening the door and signaling for students to approach.
Turning on the alternating red lights.
Pulling over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and signaling for students to approach.
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, the driver should make sure all traffic has stopped before opening the door and signaling students to board.
